entries.title: Decision gate honours the automated verdict
construct: Read every documented rule that says a recorded verdict, score, flag or eligibility result constrains a later commit action, and name the commit endpoint that must honour it
Arrange an entity whose recorded verdict is NEGATIVE by the documented rule, using the smallest legitimate input that produces it
Drive the commit action anyway with the actor the contract permits, then drive every downstream commit the entity unlocks
Arrange the mirror case with a POSITIVE verdict and drive the same commit, so an accepted commit is proof of the gate's absence rather than of a broken actor
oracles: A commit that the documented rule forbids is rejected on the rule, not merely on role, state or ownership
The verdict that gates the commit is read from the entity, quoted in the report, and matched against the documented threshold rather than assumed

entries.title: Terminal state leaves every working queue and list
construct: Enumerate every terminal and closed state of the entity from the documented state machine, and every list, queue, counter and dashboard any role reads
Arrange one entity per terminal state through the legitimate transition that reaches it
Re-read every list and aggregate as every role, unfiltered and with each documented filter, and record whether the terminal entity is present
Compare the runtime's accepted filter values against the documented enum: an undeclared value the runtime accepts marks a list whose scope is wider than the contract
oracles: A work queue contains only the states the documentation says require action; a terminal entity present in it is a defect even when every control on its row is correctly disabled
A row rendered as read-only is not evidence of correct scope: the question is whether the row belongs in the response at all

entries.title: Concurrent commit on the decision endpoint by the same actor
construct: List every endpoint that commits an irreversible decision or moves an entity into a terminal state, and treat each as its own race target: an acquire or claim endpoint tested for races does not cover the decide endpoint
Arrange one entity in the exact pre-state the commit requires, with the same authorised actor for both requests
Fire N genuinely parallel requests with no intervening read, using conflicting payloads where the contract allows a choice, so a lost update is visible as two different recorded outcomes
Re-read the entity and its full transition history, and count committed transitions rather than HTTP successes
oracles: At most one commit takes effect: exactly one transition is recorded and the entity holds one outcome
Two success responses, two history rows, or two contradictory recorded decisions are the defect, whatever the status codes were

entries.title: Post-configuration-change re-evaluation of in-flight entities
construct: Identify every configuration a privileged role can change that feeds a rule applied to existing entities: rate, threshold, limit, price, quota, eligibility parameter
Arrange three entities against one configuration value: one still in flight, one already decided, one already terminal
Change the configuration through the supported administrative path, then re-read all three entities and drive the next commit transition on the in-flight one
Assert the three oracles separately and file each violation as its own finding
oracles: Decided and terminal entities keep their recorded terms unchanged
An in-flight entity that no longer meets the new criteria is re-evaluated or visibly flagged
The commit transition re-checks the current criteria and is blocked or warned for an entity that now fails the rule
Live recomputation of a displayed value is never accepted as covering these three oracles, and no oracle may be narrowed away as out of scope

entries.title: Scope of every cardinality rule: vary the actor, not the count
construct: For every documented once, at most N, only the assigned, or per-period rule, quote the rule's scope noun first: per entity, per actor, per role, per period
Exhaust the limit on the documented scope with one actor, confirming the rule binds at all
Hold the documented scope fixed and vary every other dimension in turn: a second actor in the same role, a second entity, a later period, a reassignment of ownership
Where a legitimate path to a second actor does not exist, use a confirmed reassignment or claim defect as the arrangement step and cite it
oracles: The limit binds on the documented scope and only there: a per-entity rule that resets when the actor changes, or a per-actor rule that leaks across entities, is the defect
Reporting the existence of the limit is not a finding; the finding is the dimension on which it fails to bind
A rule exercised with a single actor is uncovered, never clean

entries.title: Exact-boundary lifecycle state construction
construct: Read the rule's exact wording and constant from the requirements, recording whether the edge is inclusive or exclusive and what the domain's smallest step is
Arrange the exact boundary state through legitimate features rather than probing whatever reachable value exists
Drive B-minus-step, B, and B-plus-step at the state level, where the step is one unit of the domain and never a blind integer increment
Assert both the accept/reject flip and the transition or side-effect the rule governs
oracles: Acceptance flips at exactly the documented mark, and the governed transition fires or is refused accordingly
An HTTP status alone is not the oracle: the recorded state after the call is

entries.title: Money and quantity recalculation after a later mutation
construct: Apply a monetary or quantitative modifier that the documentation keys on a qualifying condition
Mutate the entity afterwards so it crosses the qualifying edge in each direction
Re-read every derived amount from present state, at the smallest unit the domain uses
Check the composition invariant after every mutation, not only at the end
oracles: A modifier recomputes from current state: it appears when the entity becomes eligible and is revoked when it stops being eligible
Derived totals equal the sum of their parts with no drift, and no combination of modifiers produces a value the documentation forbids

entries.title: Commit-once under replay and double submission
construct: Enumerate every commit-style transition the journey performs and every side effect each one fires
Replay each commit twice with no intervening state read, both sequentially and in parallel
Where the contract declares an idempotency key, replay with the same key and with a fresh one, and compare
Count the entities, records and side effects created rather than reading the response body
oracles: Exactly one entity, one recorded transition and one side effect per commit, whatever the client did
A second call is rejected on the state machine, and a declared idempotency key is honoured

entries.title: Contention on the last unit of a scarce resource
construct: Discover the capacity constant from the documentation or recon rather than assuming one
Arrange the resource down to exactly one remaining unit
Fire N genuinely parallel acquisition requests from distinct actors
Re-read the resource and every derived count afterwards
oracles: At most one acquisition succeeds and no derived count exceeds the documented capacity
A queue or waiting position, where documented, holds no duplicate entry for the same actor

entries.title: Forbidden transition rejected without moving state
construct: Build the documented state machine as a decision table of pre-state by event, including the actor permitted for each edge
Drive every forbidden edge, including reversals out of terminal states and repeats of a completed transition
Re-read the entity after each rejected call and compare the recorded state and history against the pre-state
Drive every permitted edge as the control case, so a rejection is evidence of a guard rather than of a broken arrangement
oracles: A forbidden transition leaves the recorded state and history untouched and returns a message naming the rule or field, not a generic error
A permitted transition moves the state and fires its documented side effects exactly once

entries.title: Deleted or withdrawn entity does not resurface
construct: Perform the documented delete, cancel or withdraw path and confirm it reports success
Re-read the entity directly and through every list, search, export, counter and aggregate that could surface it, as every role
For principal-like entities, attempt to authenticate or act as the removed principal
Attempt each transition the entity supported before removal
oracles: The entity is absent from every surface that should no longer carry it and cannot be transitioned or authenticated
Every dependent count reflects the removal at the smallest unit

entries.title: Cross-layer divergence pinned to the documented source
construct: For every business value a user can see in more than one place, compute the documented expectation independently from the requirements before reading any layer
Record the value each layer returns for one identical input: interface, service response, stored record
Compare each layer against the independent expectation, never against another layer
Where a layer applies a factor, rounding or transformation, find its authority in the documentation and quote it or record that none exists
oracles: The layer that contradicts the documented formula carries the defect; agreement between two wrong layers is not correctness

Where the documentation is silent or ambiguous about which layer is authoritative, file both directions as separate candidates and say the direction is unresolved, rather than picking the convenient one
Three disagreeing values are three hypotheses, not one odd layer out

entries.title: Authorisation at every role-transition seam
construct: Map every handoff where the journey crosses roles and list the actions each role may take at that point
Drive each action as the role that owns it, as a peer in the same role who does not own the entity, and as a role from another part of the system
Include read, list, download and export paths, not only write paths
Repeat the peer case after a legitimate reassignment, so ownership checks are tested against a moving owner
oracles: Every action is permitted exactly for the actors the documentation names, at every seam
A peer in the same role who does not own the entity is refused on ownership, and the refusal survives reassignment

entries.title: Dependent aggregates recompute after every state event
construct: List every counter, total, percentage, remaining-capacity figure and status summary the documentation defines, and the events that should move each
Record each aggregate before the event, drive the event, and record it again
Read the aggregate through every surface that exposes it, including any cached or summary endpoint
Drive the reversing event where one exists and check the aggregate returns
oracles: Every dependent aggregate reflects the new state at the smallest unit, on every surface, with no stale or orphaned value
An aggregate defined by no documented formula is a documentation gap to file, not a value to accept

entries.title: Documented rule with an unreachable producer still gets a scenario
construct: List every documented business rule whose producer is an internal component you cannot reach: a private service, a scheduler, a queue, a database job
For each, find the observable edge that is reachable: the field the producer writes into a response, the transition it is supposed to constrain, the record it stamps
Arrange the entity so the observable value takes each documented branch, using legitimate inputs that move it, and drive the consumer behaviour at that edge
Where no observable edge exists at all, record the surface as unreachable with evidence, naming the specific surface and not the rule
oracles: A rule whose consumer behaviour is observable has a scenario, however unreachable its producer is
An unreachable dependency justifies excluding that dependency's own surface, never the rule it feeds, and never a whole risk class

entries.title: The same fact agrees across every screen of the journey
construct: Pick the facts the journey repeats: price, remaining capacity, progress, status, rating, computed terms
Walk the journey end to end and record each fact at every screen and endpoint that shows it
Drive a change that should move the fact, then walk the journey again
Include summary, list, detail and confirmation surfaces, which is where stale aggregates hide
oracles: The same fact reads identically everywhere at the smallest unit, before and after the change
A stale cached aggregate disagreeing with the live value is a defect, not a rendering delay, unless the documentation defines a staleness window

entries.title: A notifying state event notifies each recipient exactly once
construct: List every state event the documentation says must notify, by email, in-app message, push, SMS or outbound webhook, with its documented recipients, the events that must stay silent, and the channel on which Kalchas's recon says the notification is observable
Record every recipient's notification count on that channel, drive the notifying event once through the legitimate path, and record the counts again
Reach the same event through every path that produces it, then drive the repeating and reversing transitions and a rejected attempt that must not notify
Count delivered notifications per recipient per event and read the entity and state each one names, rather than trusting the response of the triggering call
oracles: Every notifying event delivers exactly one notification per documented recipient: zero is a missed notification and two is a duplicate, and each is a defect whatever the status code was
A rejected, repeated or reversed transition the documentation does not name as notifying delivers nothing, and no notification reaches an actor outside the documented recipients
The notification names the entity and the state the event produced, never a stale value or another entity's value
A channel that exists but cannot be observed from any reachable surface is a gap naming the channel, never executed on the strength of a success response

entries.title: Every recorded action writes its audit record with the real actor
construct: List every mutating and decision action that the documentation, a stated compliance requirement or the product's own audit, history or activity surface says is recorded, and the fields each record must carry: actor, action, target, time, before and after values, reason
Read the entity before the action, drive the action once as a known actor, and read the entity again, so the expected record is derived from observed state rather than from the record itself
Include a rejected attempt, an action on an entity another actor owns, and an action performed on another principal's behalf wherever the product supports delegation or impersonation
Read the record through every surface that exposes it, as each role the documentation lets read it, and offer every edit or delete path any role is shown
oracles: Each recorded action writes exactly one audit record naming the real actor, the target and before and after values that match the state read around the action

A delegated or impersonated action records both the acting and the represented principal where the documentation requires it, and a rejected attempt is recorded or omitted as documented but never recorded as a success
A missing, duplicated, misattributed or afterwards editable audit record is a defect; an audit read or tamper path open to the wrong role also routes to Perseus via Odysseus

entries.title: Exports and reports contain exactly the rows the current state permits
construct: List every export, CSV or spreadsheet download, generated report and scheduled report, with the roles, filters and date ranges the documentation says bound its rows and columns

Compute the expected row set from the state you arranged before generating anything: entities in every lifecycle state, one just inside and one just outside each filter, and another role's or tenant's entity
Generate the export as each permitted role and compare it row by row with the computed set and with the list view for the same filter
Mutate, delete and terminate entities, generate the export again, and compare counts, totals and money columns at the smallest unit
oracles: The export holds exactly the permitted rows: a missing row is an incompleteness defect, and a deleted, terminal-excluded, stale or out-of-scope row is a leak, whatever the list view shows
Every exported value equals the current application value at the smallest unit; a stale snapshot is a defect unless the documentation declares its time and the file states it

Another principal's rows in your own export stay a journey finding with the per-object authorization root routed to Perseus, and formula or CSV injection through exported cells is the security half that routes to Perseus via Odysseus

entries.title: A queued or scheduled job produces its documented effect
construct: List every effect the documentation assigns to a queued, deferred or scheduled job, such as a reminder, expiry, auto-close, recurring charge, digest, generated report or cleanup, with its trigger, its documented schedule or latency, and the observable edge where the effect lands

Arrange one entity that qualifies for the job and one control entity that does not, then trigger the job through a legitimate path: the user action that enqueues it, the documented schedule, or a run-now control the product exposes to an authorised role
Poll the observable edge with bounded waits across the documented window rather than one fixed sleep, and record when the effect lands
Trigger the job a second time, and let a second scheduled window pass where the product allows it, so a double run or an effect on the control entity becomes visible
oracles: The documented effect lands on every qualifying entity within the documented window and on no control entity
The job runs exactly once per trigger: a skipped run, a second run or an effect that never lands is a defect
Where the documentation gives no window, the elapsed time is evidence and a missing effect after a bounded wait is filed as suspected with the confirmer named
Changing the clock, editing the database or altering scheduler configuration is never an arrangement; a job that cannot be triggered or awaited legitimately is a gap naming the job

entries.title: A failed job is visible and never silently dropped
construct: For every job listed under ARI-T20, find a legitimate input that makes it fail: its target entity is deleted, cancelled or moved to a terminal state before it runs, a referenced record or recipient becomes invalid, or a documented limit is exceeded
Arrange that input, trigger the job, and read the entity status, any job or task status surface, the user-facing message, the operator view and the audit record wherever each exists
Where the documentation declares retries, count the attempts and read the final state after the last one
Leave failures that need injected faults, killed workers or broker outages to Tyche, and message-protocol poison handling to Proteus, and route any you observe via Odysseus
oracles: A failed job leaves a visible failed state, error, retry marker or alert on a surface the documentation names; a failure visible nowhere is a silently dropped job and a defect
A failed job applies no partial effect, or flags the partial effect as recoverable the way the documentation says, and never shows the entity as completed
Documented retries stop at their bound, and a job the documentation says is retried is never abandoned after its first failure
